name: Play a recognizable melody on piano
blurb: Any keyboard, a bit of geography, and one tune played properly with both hands. Far more satisfying than a month of scales.
gear: A simple sheet or a note-by-note tutorial
steps: Learn the keyboard layout: find middle C by the pattern of two and three black keys, and learn to locate any note quickly.
Learn correct hand shape — curved fingers, relaxed wrist, fingertips on the keys — before playing anything.
Learn a simple right-hand melody in C major, hands separate, slowly, counting out loud.
Add a simple left-hand accompaniment: single root notes on the beat, then broken chords.
Put hands together at half speed and only raise the tempo when it is completely clean.
Memorise the piece so you can play it for someone without the sheet.
tips: Practise the two-bar section you keep fluffing, not the whole piece. Repetition of the whole thing is mostly rehearsing the parts you already have.
Use a metronome from the start; playing rubato is a choice, not an accident.
proof: You play a recognisable tune with both hands, from memory, at a steady tempo.
